title: Reduce complete weighted-path replay time by 8.94% (no κ)
body:
## Summary

A new row-sparse Gaussian evaluator reduces the complete retained PR800 `verify.py` command's median wall time by **8.94%**, while preserving its entire scientific output and every check in that entry point. It omits exactly **1,237,016 zero Gaussian products** on cache misses. Claim type: scoped implementation-preservation proof, exact finite conformance and local performance evidence. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

```diff
 complete PR800 replay
- visit eight right-hand columns for every nonzero left coefficient
+ visit only nonzero entries of the corresponding right-hand row
  unchanged normalization, phase convention, cache capacity and consumer
```

Only `research/sparse-gaussian-path-replay/` is added. The original scientific results are cited premises, not an audit deliverable. Credit Jeremy Diviney / jeremydiviney PR800 for the weighted-path theorem, certificates and complete replay; Ivan / littleBro PR705 and PR680 for the corpus, screen and exact dense/symbolic engines; eumemic PR288, Swapnil Jain and the retained Clifford lineage. Sparse multiplication is classical. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19362386) preceded implementation and conformance work. The first verified improvement is shipped without extending to another consumer.

## Evidence

Before, the complete replay evaluates 2,275,392 Gaussian numerator products on 8,164 cache misses. After, it evaluates 1,038,376. All **30,343 reached requests**, including **22,179 hits**, agree with the original evaluator, with identical cache inventories and an ordered input/flag/result transcript. Complete scientific stdout has SHA256 `5c63fd080111bc2848c9995866905f1bc3041cd1f357cc636602dc5a15225964`.

The complete inherited workload retains its 73-word screen, nine unresolved cases, 2,187 dense paths, 919 certificates, 1,152 frame choices, 104 Laurent determinant controls, three valid nine-call controls and all rejection checks of `verify.py`. Dense conjugation and full Pauli reconstruction remain independent of symbolic tableau transitions. No result from later PR955 is replayed or claimed as new.

The new checker passes **6,625** exact kernel comparisons and **20** rejection executions: each of seventeen corrupted source inputs, an actual wrong-sign evaluator, and optimized execution of the original source and adapter. Git-free replay with empty PATH gives identical complete output. The generated stdout receipt binds all package-file hashes. Committed-byte/mode and declared-source-history preflight pass for **26 files**.

Final complete-command measurements on CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, 18 logical CPUs, five alternating fresh-process pairs:

| Command | Median seconds | Range seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Original complete replay | 0.574331250 | 0.572040000 to 0.578966791 |
| Sparse complete replay | 0.522962709 | 0.518634458 to 0.527706291 |

All ten outputs agree, with zero command errors. Both arms include startup, imports, source checks, the complete consumer and output, with strict diagnostics and fresh bytecode namespaces. Adapter authentication is included. The README preserves every raw sample. Normalization and certificate traversal remain measured costs in separate untimed profiles. This local timing is not a cross-platform promise or a CI threshold.

From the repository root, using an existing external scratch directory:

```sh
TMPDIR=/absolute/scratch /Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/sparse-gaussian-path-replay
TMPDIR=/absolute/scratch /Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/sparse-gaussian-path-replay/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/sparse-gaussian-path-replay --check-source-history
```

All passed locally, with markers `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, `PASS_SPARSE_GAUSSIAN_PATH_REPLAY` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. The registered check's exact argument array took **4.78 seconds** locally against its 120-second limit. Another CPython 3.12 path can replace the displayed interpreter; no external dependencies are required.

Optional complete measurement:

```sh
TMPDIR=/absolute/scratch /Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/sparse-gaussian-path-replay/benchmark.py --output /absolute/scratch/measurement.json
```

The output path must be new and outside the checkout. That generated measurement binds the executed evaluator, adapter, benchmark, source manifest and all seventeen immutable inputs.

## Limitations

The written equality proof covers fixed 8-by-8 exact Gaussian numerator matrices; finite conformance supports that proof. The adapter is opt-in and does not change a shared replay command. Original source assertions remain enabled; optimized scientific execution is deliberately rejected. All registered checks ran locally. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

No new mathematical exclusion, native operation, physical caller, dirty-restoration schedule, complete recursive invoice, supplier admission or multiplication theorem is supplied. No Lean, Docker, selected cold replay, native suite, original `validate.py` packaging harness or PR955 scientific replay was run. The current selected framework assumptions retain their status.

## Open next questions

Can the same evaluator improve the distinct complete PR955 consumer? First profile that entire command and specify its input, output and failure contract, then compare every reached request and alternate complete runs. Its Boolean and polynomial work may dominate. No PR955 adapter, transcript or timing is supplied, and no continuation is reserved.

## Related open work

No open PR studying this fixed PR800 replay, its row-sparse evaluator or its exact work count was found in the refreshed open-PR, source-reference and live-claim searches. PR800 and its PR955 successor are merged predecessors with distinct scientific contributions. PR6207 is a separate quadratic Gauss-sum evaluator for a different complete consumer; this work does not answer its follow-up questions.

Coverage is bounded: the card cache reports complete remote pagination for 388 open PRs and 6,329 Discussion records, while the sparse local scan omitted 8,801 of 8,917 HEAD notes. Direct main object/algorithm searches, merged searches and the live precommit refresh supplement that cache. Unpublished work and arbitrary historical diffs remain outside coverage.

The completion refresh examined all thirteen other account open PRs created since the advance CLAIM. None computes this replay's Gaussian-product count or its complete-command timing. No additional computation checked another contribution.

- [#6443](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6443) proves a unitary Clifford correction-rank theorem. This PR changes exact Gaussian multiplication in the fixed PR800 consumer. The mathematical rank and implementation work count are different quantities; no shared numerical value is compared.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed at head `1b246be65d26be545406136c5c4ca26fd1883f85` in [run 41544520454](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41544520454): `plan` in 4m24s and `replay (research/sparse-gaussian-path-replay)` in 1m40s. The completed checks were read once; run metadata confirms completed success and the matching head. Local registered replay, direct verification and committed-byte/source-history preflight also pass. Hosted replay certifies the registered conformance checks, not a universal performance gain or scientific acceptance of predecessor claims.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** package.

Nine isolated research files and seventeen declared immutable inputs. No predecessor bytes, shared implementations or selected-frontier files change.
